reasoning: The document has a composite fidelity score of 0.7967 but suffers from several major and critical structural defects. Most notably, all 8 hyperlinks from the source document were lost, list numbering resets improperly around images, and heading hierarchy is broken. Programmatic signals also show low content preservation (shingling recall 0.693, word count ratio 0.628). These issues strictly forbid AUTO_APPROVE and require human intervention.

concerns.description: Source PDF has 8 hyperlinks but output has none — all links lost during extraction
concerns.analysis: source_link_count=8, output_link_count=0. PDF URI annotations were not preserved as link elements.

On page 2, the source document contains three column headings that are visually at the same level: 'How to reset your password', 'How to change your password', and 'How to update your profile'. The output incorrectly assigns 'How to reset your password' as an H2, but demotes the other two to H3.

concerns.output_quote: "type": "heading", "level": 2, "text": "How to reset your password" ... "type": "heading", "level": 3, "text": "How to change your password"

concerns.analysis: The source document relies on bold text formatting to emphasize user interface elements and instructions (e.g., 'Register now', 'activation link', 'Trouble Signing On?', 'Unlock Account'). In the HTML output, these strings are rendered as plain unstyled text. The only preserved bolding is on the word 'Note:', whereas the PDF bolds the entire sentence 'Note: Your account will automatically unlock after 2 hours.'

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (3): MyNCID User Guide * Ver 1.0; September 23, 2025; Page 1 of 3
concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=3. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

The source document contains single continuous numbered lists in each column, but the output breaks these into separate list objects wherever an image interrupts the text. Because there is no numbering continuation mechanism used, this results in the numbering resetting to 1 for items that should be 3, 4, 5, etc.
